A Section 4 invocation NOT sustained by both Houses does not count; impeachment without removal does not count.
An ANNOUNCEMENT of resignation/removal before Dec-31 resolves YES IMMEDIATELY, regardless of effective date — the one clause that WIDENS YES.
Resolution source is 'a consensus of credible reporting', NOT a named source — so no resolution-source-lag angle exists here, unlike the HLE family.
Impeachment resolutions H.Res.353/537/939 are INTRODUCED in the 119th Congress; none has produced a Senate removal and the majorities do not exist.

P(YES) ~1.5%. ALERT TRIAGE for the Greenland keywords added 2026-08-12: a headline about a 'deal', 'agreement' or 'framework' is NOT a thesis break unless the reporting names a BINDING instrument (enacted legislation, signed treaty, signed agreement text, or an executive action implementing one). Basing-rights headlines are noise by construction. 0.98 -> 0.95 on 2026-08-13. The STALE-SOURCE check fired on its first day for this position (203d-old source behind a criteria_read of 0 days) and immediately earned itself: refreshing found live negotiations whose SHAPE — unlimited, uncurbable exclusive access to defined areas — creeps toward the Guantanamo-style qualifying example in the criteria, a path I had dismissed when I read 'basing rights are excluded' this morning and stopped there. Still a strong NO: Denmark's sovereignty red line holds, the deal is framed as respecting it, and YES needs a BINDING instrument granting exclusive JURISDICTION rather than guaranteed access. WATCH: any reporting of signed text that displaces Danish legal authority in a defined zone, as opposed to guaranteeing US use of it.

key_facts.claim: YES requires a BINDING agreement or legal instrument producing sovereignty transfer, primary/exclusive US jurisdiction, or acquisition by force.
EXCLUDED by name: non-binding statements, negotiations, proposals, FRAMEWORKS and MOUs.
EXCLUDED by name: basing rights, access agreements, SOFA/COFA arrangements, commercial concessions, leases.
A QUALIFYING example named in the criteria is a Guantanamo-style zone under exclusive/primary US jurisdiction where Danish law does not apply except by US permission.

As of May-Jun 2026: talks ongoing, NO deal yet (Greenland PM May-12); Pentagon negotiating ACCESS to 3 new military sites; Denmark expects a deal BY YEAR-END; Danish sovereignty red line explicitly intact. An ACCESS deal is not acquisition under the criteria — but a year-end "deal" headline is an interpretation-flap risk for Q4; re-verify criteria wording vs any signed text before reacting to such a headline.

_comment_key_facts: key_facts = the load-bearing factual claims a position rests on, each paired with the EXTERNAL source it came from. Added 2026-08-11 after a prior revision inverted the direction of a source's anchor move and then survived TWO re-verifications, because each re-verification re-read my own note and reproduced the error. A re-verification that does not diff the recorded claim against the source's actual words is confirmation, not verification. The audit rotation surfaces these for source-diffing. TAGGING CAVEAT (2026-08-12): the audit tags a source UNVERIFIED when it does not start with http, but a URL that 403s (congress.gov) is no more agent-verifiable than a prose 'sweep'. Where that happens, say so INLINE in the claim and name the independent falsifier used instead — do not let an unfetchable URL launder a claim into looking checked. SOURCE_DATE (2026-08-12): distinct from `checked`. `checked` is when I last LOOKED; `source_date` is when the source was PUBLISHED. The MacBook staleness cost 18pp precisely because those diverged invisibly — checked=1d ago on a source published 114d earlier, in a story that had moved three times since. For live-state sources (a leaderboard, an order book, a market description) the two are equal by construction. ATOMICITY REQUIRED (2026-08-13): one independently checkable assertion per entry, each with its own source and source_date. Bundled entries are how an unchecked fact hides inside a checked one — SpaceX's 'No plausible 2026 rival: OpenAI pushed to 2027, and a >$2.1T close would need an S-1 already public' bundled OpenAI's TIMING (checked twice) with every other rival's SIZE (never checked), and the second cost the project its largest prior correction. If an entry contains ' and ' joining two verifiable claims, split it. SOURCE TAXONOMY (2026-08-13) — 'is it a URL' is the WRONG test and my first sweep miscategorised because of it. Ranked by what may move a number: (1) FIRST-HAND MEASUREMENT — a CLOB book walk, a gamma/API read, an on-chain balance. Reproducible on demand and STRONGER than any article, even though it carries no URL. (2) DATED PRIMARY ARTIFACT — a fetched, dated piece; the standard for a factual claim about the world. (3) NAMED BUT UNLINKED — e.g. 'third-party trackers'; verifiable with effort, acceptable if the claim is checked periodically. (4) AGGREGATED SEARCH SUMMARY — a LEAD ONLY. It must never move a prior: on 2026-08-13 one such summary said the M5 reshuffle was an 'acceleration', moved MacBook 0.62->0.58, and pinning it to dated sources REFUTED it outright. Label the kind when the source is not a URL, so a future sweep does not mistake a measurement for a guess.
_comment_divergence_ack: divergence_ack MUST be a bare ISO date string (e.g. "2026-08-15") — position_state_audit §3c parses it with date.fromisoformat() directly and treats anything else as EXPIRED via the exception path. 14-day window from that date. Put prose in divergence_ack_reason (audit ignores it). Same for source_ack. Learned 2026-08-16: two acks written as rich dicts were silently invalid; one flagged, one was a near-miss.

strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to-norm.note: DEC-0077. MECHANICAL, first-hand measured, and now a VERIFIED IMPOSSIBILITY rather than a forecast: YES needs the IMF PortWatch 7-day MA of Hormuz transit calls to reach 60 on any date through Aug-31. Latest pull (2026-08-25): 7dMA 5.00 over Aug-17..23 (prints 4,6,6,5,4,7,3; the note previously carried ~3.5 from an older window), daily prints 1-8, and the peak SINGLE DAY across 150 prints is 44 — a level never once observed, needed as a 7-day AVERAGE, inside 6 days, during an active conflict that has if anything escalated (tanker struck off Oman Aug-25; Iranian threats to neighbours Aug-23). SECOND GUARD CORRECTED 2026-08-25: the feed lag is ~2 DAYS, not the ~6 I had recorded (newest print Aug-23 pulled on Aug-25), so the publication-lag argument is WEAKER than written — data through ~Aug-29 will publish before resolution. It does not matter: the bar needs 420 transit calls in a 7-day window and the latest week delivered 35, so the fade rests on the measurement, not on the lag. Recording the correction because a guard I would have quoted as load-bearing was simply wrong. p_no 0.998 is the residual for source/resolver error, NOT for traffic. HOLD TO RESOLUTION: at mark 0.998 a taker sell captures ~nothing AND pays a fee, while resolution is fee-free — the 2026-08-25 alert's 'consider profit-taking' note was correctly declined on that math. Erosion trigger armed (hormuz-no-erosion, NO bid <=0.95). Regime caveat (2026-08-19 lesson): this near-certainty is specific to the 12-day horizon; it does NOT transfer to the Sep-30/Dec-31 siblings, which are war-duration forecasts. || FEED OPS (2026-08-25): the ArcGIS endpoint 400s TRANSIENTLY with 'Invalid query parameters' on identical params that succeed seconds later, and it REQUIRES orderByFields — a one-shot pull returns an empty feature list that naive code reads as 'no data' rather than 'query failed'. Any resolution-day check must RETRY (4x) and must distinguish empty-result from error-result. Latest series Aug-17..23: 4,6,6,5,4,7,3 -> 7dMA 5.00.
